column11: Pitolisant, the once-daily oral narcolepsy drug nearest in form: 131 of 370 adults with NT1 or NT2 (35.4%) had stopped it at the interim analysis after 42.6 months of a 5-year European post-authorisation safety study (Sleep Medicine 2025, doi 10.1016/j.sleep.2025.02.012), mainly for safety (14.3%), lack of response (8.7%) and patient decision (7.6%). At a constant hazard over that window, 1 - 0.646^(12/42.6) = 11.58% a year. Enrolment was staggered, so the average patient was followed for less than 42.6 months and the true annual rate is higher: this is a floor. A 2020 Avadel release put first-year stopping on twice-nightly sodium oxybate near 50%, a harder regimen

The best fit is a step, new starts at their plateau from the first full year (midpoint -3.0 and k 4.0 at the edge of the grid; rmse 8.3% of the 2025 level): Wakix's Medicare stock grew almost linearly, which at this stopping rate is a flat rate of new starts from launch. Xywav (November 2020) gives the same front-loaded shape at this rate: new starts of 744 in 2021, then 267, 390, 293 and 409. At 35.4% stopping the Wakix fit stays front-loaded but sits on the grid's floor for k (midpoint -1.7, k 0.2, rmse 6.0%); with k free below 0.2 a near-linear climb in new starts fits marginally better (rmse 5.8%). Medicare is a small share of narcolepsy, whose patients are mostly under 65
